newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan gets nod to form Vietnam car venture.
newsitem.headline: Nissan gets nod to form Vietnam car venture.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday that it had obtained approval from the Vietnamese government to form a joint venture for the manufacture of vehicles in Vietnam.
The joint venture will be formed soon, Nissan said.
Nissan TCM Vietnam Co Ltd, to be capitalised at $18 million, would be 75 percent owned by Nissan TCM Pty Ltd and 25 percent by Danang Automobile Mechanical Factory, Nissan said in a statement.
Nissan TCM is a joint investment firm formed in 1995. It is owned by Nissan, Japanese trading house Marubeni Corp and Tan Chong & Sons Motor Co Sdn Bhd, Nissan's Malaysian arm.

Construction of a new plant will begin in the Hoa Khanh Industrial Park near the city of Danang early next year and the plant will start producing Sunny compact sedans and Vanette commercial vans in the summer of 1998, Nissan said.
Initial output is expected to total 1,000 units, Nissan said.
